summary: The article uses the September 14, 2023 Buckman Bridge collapse in Jacksonville as a starting point to examine how technology could make public works safer. It covers structural health monitoring sensors, digital twins, self-healing materials and new construction methods, then turns to legislative hurdles, public-private partnerships and workforce training. It concludes that merging technology with infrastructure is an urgent priority requiring a collaborative approach.
one_line: After the Buckman Bridge collapse, the article explores how sensors, digital twins, smart materials, policy, partnerships and training could improve public infrastructure safety.
key_facts: The Buckman Bridge in Jacksonville collapsed on September 14, 2023, which prompted national questions about the resilience of public works.
Experts described the Buckman Bridge failure as a cascade failure, caused by a mix of overlooked maintenance issues and environmental wear.
On October 5, 2023, at the American Society of Civil Engineers' conference, Dr. Linda Hayes unveiled research on structural health monitoring systems.
Hayes's monitoring systems use sensors from fiber optics to piezoelectric devices to detect stress, corrosion and microscopic fissures in concrete and steel.

A digital twin is a virtual replica of a physical entity used to simulate and analyze its behavior under various conditions; the concept was highlighted at the Oliver Thompson lecture on September 30, 2023.
At the Future of Public Works Expo on November 19, 2023, self-healing bio-concrete laced with bacteria that produce limestone to fill cracks was showcased.
The same Future of Public Works Expo unveiled construction advances such as robotic automation and 3D printing.
Council member Sarah Johnson, interviewed on December 1, 2023, expressed trepidation about implementation costs and the renegotiation of accountability when machinery can predict disasters.
Advocates of tech integration argue that initial costs will be small compared with the economic and human toll of infrastructure failures.
Springfield mayor Michael Patterson announced on December 22, 2023 an initiative to foster partnerships with tech companies specializing in smart infrastructure solutions.
Public-private partnerships raise dilemmas such as the ethical use of collected data and spreading benefits across socio-economic divides.
Civil engineer Jennifer Gonzalez stressed at a January 8, 2024 workshop that the workforce must be continually educated and adapted to technological shifts.
